project.name: health_tracker
detection_signals: pubspec.yaml depends on the Flutter SDK

summary.headline: 5 issue(s) with clear evidence must be fixed before release

findings.title: targetSdk 34 is below Google Play's requirement (API 36)
findings.explanation: Since 2026-08-31, new apps and app updates (phone-tablet) must target API level 36 or higher to be submitted. Play Console will reject this upload.
findings.recommendation: Raise targetSdk to 36 or higher, review the Android behavior changes for each version you skip, and update plugins that pin older SDKs.

references.title: Meet Google Play's target API level requirement
Target API level requirements for Google Play apps (Play Console Help)

findings.title: Android application ID uses the reserved prefix "com.example" (com.example.health_tracker)
findings.explanation: Google Play does not accept packages that start with com.example. The application ID is permanent once the app is published.
findings.recommendation: Choose a reverse-domain ID you own (e.g. com.yourcompany.app), set applicationId, and update namespace, MainActivity package and Firebase/Google config files to match.

references.title: Configure the app module (application ID)

findings.title: Version name "1.3.0-beta" is not a valid App Store version
findings.explanation: Version name must be one to three period-separated integers (e.g. 1.4.2). App Store Connect rejects uploads with suffixes such as -beta or letters.
findings.recommendation: Use a plain numeric version (e.g. 1.4.2) and put pre-release labels in the build number or release notes instead.

references.title: CFBundleShortVersionString

findings.title: Empty purpose string: NSCameraUsageDescription
findings.explanation: NSCameraUsageDescription is declared but has no text. iOS shows this string in the permission prompt, and App Review rejects prompts that do not explain the purpose.
findings.recommendation: Write a specific sentence describing what the app does with this access, e.g. "Scan receipts to add expenses." Remove the key if the feature does not exist.

references.title: App Review Guidelines 5.1.1 – Data Collection and Storage
Information Property List (purpose strings / usage descriptions)

findings.title: Release build is signed with the debug key
findings.explanation: The release build type uses signingConfigs.debug (the default in new Flutter projects). Google Play rejects bundles signed with a debug certificate, and the debug key is not yours to keep.
findings.recommendation: Create an upload keystore, reference it from a release signingConfig loaded from key.properties (kept out of git), and enroll in Play App Signing.

references.title: Sign your app

findings.title: Required reason APIs used without an app privacy manifest
findings.explanation: App-owned iOS code appears to use User defaults APIs, but no PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy was found. Apple requires apps to declare approved reasons for these APIs; uploads without them receive ITMS-91053.
findings.recommendation: Add PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy to the app target (Xcode: File > New > File > App Privacy) and declare each category with the reason code that matches your use.

references.title: Describing use of required reason API
Privacy manifest files

findings.title: No web account deletion URL declared
findings.explanation: Google Play requires apps that allow account creation to provide a web link where users can request account and data deletion without reinstalling the app. The link is entered in the Data safety form; the scanner cannot see Play Console, so it relies on your declaration.
findings.recommendation: Publish a page that explains how to request deletion (and what data is deleted or retained), enter it in Play Console > App content > Data safety, and record it as app.account_deletion.web_url.

references.title: Understanding Google Play's app account deletion requirements
Provide information for Google Play's Data safety section

findings.title: Background location requires a Play Console declaration and review
findings.explanation: Apps that access location in the background must show the feature is core to the app, provide a prominent in-app disclosure, and submit the location permissions declaration with a video. Requested: ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION.
findings.recommendation: Remove background location unless it is essential. If it is, prepare the declaration form, a demo video, and the prominent disclosure before submitting.

references.title: Requesting access to location in the background

findings.title: Broad photo/video access needs a qualifying use or the photo picker
findings.explanation: Under Google Play's Photo and Video Permissions policy, only apps whose core functionality needs broad access to photos/videos may request READ_MEDIA_IMAGES/READ_MEDIA_VIDEO, and they must declare it. Apps with occasional needs must use the Android photo picker. Requested: READ_MEDIA_IMAGES.
findings.recommendation: Switch to the system photo picker (image_picker on recent versions uses it) and remove the permissions, or submit the declaration if broad access is core.

references.title: Google Play's Photo and Video Permissions policy

findings.title: App appears to create accounts but no in-app deletion flow was found
findings.explanation: Both Apple (Guideline 5.1.1(v)) and Google Play require apps that support account creation to let users initiate account deletion from within the app. The scanner found account-creation signals but no deletion flow.
findings.recommendation: Add a clearly labelled “Delete account” action (e.g. in Settings > Account) that deletes the account and associated data, then record the path in .release-doctor.yml (app.account_deletion.in_app_path).

references.title: Offering account deletion in your app
App Review Guidelines 5.1.1 – Data Collection and Storage
Understanding Google Play's app account deletion requirements

findings.title: iOS bundle identifier is still the template value (com.example.healthTracker)
findings.explanation: com.example identifiers come from project templates. The bundle ID must match an App ID registered to your team and cannot be changed after release.
findings.recommendation: Register your own bundle ID in the Apple Developer portal and set PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER for the app target and its extensions.

references.title: App Review Guidelines

findings.title: Signing passwords in android/key.properties
findings.explanation: key.properties holds the upload keystore passwords. It should stay out of version control.
findings.recommendation: Add key.properties to .gitignore, remove it from git history, and rotate the passwords if they were pushed.

references.title: App Review Guidelines 5.1.1 – Data Collection and Storage
User Data policy (privacy policy requirements)

findings.title: App still contains the Flutter counter template
findings.explanation: Template screens indicate the app may be incomplete. Apple rejects incomplete apps (Guideline 2.1) and apps with minimal functionality (4.2); Google Play has a similar minimum functionality policy.

evidence.value: home: const MyHomePage(title: 'Flutter Demo Home Page'),
const Text('You have pushed the button this many times:'),

findings.recommendation: Remove the template screen and make sure the release build opens to real app content.

references.title: App Review Guidelines 2.1 – App Completeness
App Review Guidelines 4.2 – Minimum Functionality
Spam and Minimum Functionality policy

findings.title: Privacy policy URL looks like a placeholder
findings.explanation: "https://example.com/privacy" does not look like a real, public policy page.
findings.recommendation: Replace it with the public URL of your privacy policy.

references.title: App Review Guidelines 5.1.1 – Data Collection and Storage
App privacy details on the App Store
User Data policy (privacy policy requirements)
Provide information for Google Play's Data safety section

findings.title: Purpose string needs review: NSContactsUsageDescription
findings.explanation: The text for NSContactsUsageDescription does not explain how the app uses the data. Apple expects the prompt to state clearly and completely why the app needs the access.

evidence.value: This app needs access to your contacts

findings.recommendation: Describe the concrete feature that uses this access, in the language of the app's UI, and localize it via InfoPlist.strings when the app is localized.

references.title: App Review Guidelines 5.1.1 – Data Collection and Storage
Information Property List (purpose strings / usage descriptions)

findings.title: Purpose string needs review: NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription
findings.explanation: The text for NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription is too short to explain the purpose. Apple expects the prompt to state clearly and completely why the app needs the access.
findings.recommendation: Describe the concrete feature that uses this access, in the language of the app's UI, and localize it via InfoPlist.strings when the app is localized.

references.title: App Review Guidelines 5.1.1 – Data Collection and Storage
Information Property List (purpose strings / usage descriptions)

findings.title: Cleartext (HTTP) traffic is allowed for all domains
findings.explanation: android:usesCleartextTraffic="true" in src/main enables unencrypted traffic in release builds.
findings.recommendation: Remove it, or use a network security config that allows cleartext only for the specific domains that need it (and only in debug if possible).

references.title: Security risk: cleartext communications

findings.title: App Transport Security is disabled (NSAllowsArbitraryLoads)
findings.explanation: NSAllowsArbitraryLoads turns off HTTPS enforcement for all connections. App Review may ask for a justification, and it is often a leftover from development.
findings.recommendation: Remove it and add NSExceptionDomains only for hosts that cannot use HTTPS, or move the exception to a debug-only Info.plist.

references.title: NSAppTransportSecurity

findings.title: Possible hard-coded secret "backendApiSecret" in lib/config.dart
findings.explanation: A credential-like name is assigned a literal value. It may be a real secret or a harmless identifier; the scanner cannot tell.
findings.recommendation: If it is a secret, move it to your backend or a CI secret. If it is public by design, add an ignore entry with the reason in .release-doctor.yml.

references.title: App Review Guidelines 5.1.1 – Data Collection and Storage
User Data policy (privacy policy requirements)

findings.title: Lorem ipsum placeholder text found
findings.explanation: Placeholder text in shipped screens is a common App Completeness rejection reason. Matches in unused code or tests are harmless.

evidence.value: const Text('Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet'),

findings.recommendation: Replace placeholder text with final copy, or confirm these strings are not reachable in the release build.

references.title: App Review Guidelines 2.1 – App Completeness
App Review Guidelines 4.2 – Minimum Functionality
Spam and Minimum Functionality policy

findings.title: Privacy policy may not cover Google Analytics for Firebase
findings.explanation: The project includes firebase_analytics (analytics), but privacy-policy.md does not mention it or its purpose. The SDK's actual data collection depends on how it is configured.
findings.recommendation: Check Google Analytics for Firebase's data disclosure documentation and your configuration, then describe the data, purpose and recipient in the policy, App Privacy details and Data safety form.

references.title: App Review Guidelines 5.1.1 – Data Collection and Storage
App privacy details on the App Store
User Data policy (privacy policy requirements)
Provide information for Google Play's Data safety section

findings.title: Hard-coded versionName overrides pubspec.yaml
findings.explanation: build.gradle sets versionName "1.3.0" but pubspec.yaml says 1.3.0-beta.
findings.recommendation: Use `versionName flutter.versionName`.

references.title: Version your app

findings.title: Hard-coded versionCode overrides pubspec.yaml
findings.explanation: build.gradle sets versionCode 3, but pubspec.yaml says build 7. Bumping pubspec.yaml will not change the Android build, which leads to "version code already used" upload errors.
findings.recommendation: Use `versionCode flutter.versionCode` (Groovy) or `versionCode = flutter.versionCode` (Kotlin DSL).

references.title: Version your app

findings.title: Photo library permission may be unnecessary
findings.explanation: The app declares photo library access, but the scanner found no known photo library dependency or API call in the scanned sources. This needs verification; it is not proof of a policy violation.

evidence.description: No photo library dependency or API usage found in 4 scanned source file(s)

findings.recommendation: Confirm which feature or dependency uses photo library. If none does, remove the permission and its purpose string; both stores reject or question permissions the app does not need.

references.title: App Review Guidelines 5.1.1 – Data Collection and Storage
Permissions and APIs that Access Sensitive Information

findings.title: Contacts permission may be unnecessary
findings.explanation: The app declares contacts access, but the scanner found no known contacts dependency or API call in the scanned sources. This needs verification; it is not proof of a policy violation.

evidence.description: No contacts dependency or API usage found in 4 scanned source file(s)

findings.recommendation: Confirm which feature or dependency uses contacts. If none does, remove the permission and its purpose string; both stores reject or question permissions the app does not need.

references.title: App Review Guidelines 5.1.1 – Data Collection and Storage

findings.title: Confirm reviewers can sign in
findings.explanation: The app appears to have accounts. If any feature requires signing in, reviewers need working credentials or a demo mode.
findings.recommendation: Set app.requires_login_for_review and app.review_demo_account_provided in .release-doctor.yml after preparing the reviewer account.

references.title: App Review Guidelines 2.1 – App Completeness

findings.title: Launcher label looks like a package name ("health_tracker")
findings.explanation: Project templates set the launcher label to the project's snake_case name; it is what users see under the icon.
findings.recommendation: Set android:label to the app's display name (or a @string resource).

references.title: App Review Guidelines 2.1 – App Completeness
App Review Guidelines 4.2 – Minimum Functionality
Spam and Minimum Functionality policy

findings.title: Permissions that must be reflected in the Data safety form
findings.explanation: The app requests ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, CAMERA. If the app collects or shares the related data, the Data safety form must disclose it.
findings.recommendation: For each permission, decide which data type it produces (e.g. precise location, photos, audio), whether it leaves the device, and declare it in Play Console > App content > Data safety.

references.title: Provide information for Google Play's Data safety section

findings.title: Unfinished-feature labels found
findings.explanation: Labels such as “Coming soon” suggest features that reviewers cannot use. Reviewers may treat visible placeholders as incomplete functionality.
findings.recommendation: Hide unfinished features in release builds (feature flags) rather than showing placeholder screens or buttons.

references.title: App Review Guidelines 2.1 – App Completeness
App Review Guidelines 4.2 – Minimum Functionality

rule_results.title: Web link for account deletion requests is declared
Sensitive Android permissions have a policy path
targetSdk meets Google Play's current requirement
Permission purpose strings are present and specific
Required reason APIs are declared in the privacy manifest
Apps with account creation offer in-app account deletion
Application ID and bundle identifier are not template values
Release builds do not use debug configuration
No credentials embedded in the project
Declared permissions have a matching feature
Privacy policy is available and covers detected SDKs
Version name and build number are valid and consistent

disclaimer: Automated checks cannot guarantee App Store or Google Play approval. Passing rules mean no issue was detected with the available evidence; items marked needs_review require a human decision.
